A1.justification: The title, authors, FCI/PAG approach, simulation, and bird experiment clearly identify the same work. All supplied text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable. v1's supplemental sections are absent from the supplied v2, although v2 still references supplementary material.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 report original synthetic-image experiments and bird-classification results, including classifier accuracy and bootstrapped causal-edge frequencies.

after.justification: Sections IV–V retain original simulation and bird results and add pneumonia-classification experiments with accuracy, edge-stability results, and an estimated causal graph.

M1.justification: Both versions use FCI to learn a PAG over interpretable features and predictions, allowing latent confounding and constraining predictions to be non-ancestors of the features. ResNet18 remains the prediction architecture. The X-ray application uses the same proposed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds binary pneumonia detection using ChestX-ray8 images and radiologist findings, substantially extending evaluation into medical imaging. The synthetic-shape and Caltech-UCSD bird tasks remain.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparisons against alternative explanation or causal-discovery methods. CXPlain, neural-network causal attribution, PC, and other approaches are discussed as related work rather than evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: v2 counts both directed and partially directed edges in reported causal-edge frequencies; v1 counts partially directed edges. The new X-ray protocol uses 239 images, seven binary findings, 50 reserved test images, FCI alpha 0.05, and unrestricted conditioning-set size. The stated bird splits, alpha, and conditioning limit remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a qualitative examination of an individual X-ray bootstrap PAG in Figure 6, displaying confounding relationships and the connections between clinical findings and predictions alongside aggregate edge stabilities. The synthetic hidden-confounder illustration remains unchanged; no new ablation or robustness test is reported.

E5.justification: The reported bird bootstrap count increases from 40 to 50, and v2 specifies 100 bootstrap replicates for X-rays. Relative edge frequency remains the uncertainty-related reporting approach, now explicitly described as edge stability.

E6.justification: v2 replaces the bird edge-frequency results: v1 Table 1 highlights size, bill length, bill shape, and eye color, while v2 Figure 5 ranks size, eye color, and bill shape highest. These use revised bootstrap and edge-counting settings. v2 also adds 74.55% X-ray accuracy and strong edge stabilities for infiltration, atelectasis, and effusion. Simulation accuracy of 81% and bird accuracy of 86.57% remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly introduces faithfulness and adds mathematical definitions of observational and causal image classes, followed by the argument that these classes coincide for deterministic predictions. It also states a large-sample implication of FCI's established properties. v1's brief definition of causal-effect identification is omitted.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same central contribution: using causal structure learning over interpretable features to distinguish possible causes of predictions from confounded associations and support algorithm auditing. The new application expands supporting evidence without redefining that contribution.

C2.justification: v1 leaves combining causal feature extraction with the proposal as future work. v2 substantially revises this outlook: deterministic predictions collapse observational and causal classes, image manipulations do not supply reusable interpretable labels, and alternative feature extractors require annotations or produce opaque representations. This materially sharpens applicability limits and the role of human feature selection.

D1.justification: v1's supplements provide exact bird-category and attribute mappings, missing-value codes, and training details including cross-entropy, SGD, learning rate, momentum, and decay schedule. These sections are absent from the supplied v2 despite retained supplement references. v2 adds X-ray sampling and label-construction details. This changes the documentation supplied, without establishing changes to bird training.

R1.justification: Section VI.C expands a brief future-work connection into substantive comparisons with causal feature learning, Lopez-Paz et al.'s object-based features, and unsupervised image representations. Additional PAG-learning and counterfactual visual-explanation references broaden the context, while the identification-overview reference is removed. The main change is the revised positioning concerning automatic feature extraction.

P1.justification: The seven-section narrative and much of the existing prose remain. Local rewrites clarify FCI and feature consolidation, the experimental-section heading expands to cover both applications, and author affiliations are updated. The supplemental sections are omitted.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. The bird-results table becomes part of the ranked two-panel Figure 5; v2 adds a PAG-edge interpretation table, an X-ray example, and an X-ray PAG. Existing bird and synthetic illustrations are retained with resizing and relocation.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens empirical support with the pneumonia application and substantially improves the explanation of feature-selection limitations. However, the supplied PDF loses the detailed bird preprocessing and training supplements while continuing to reference them, reducing reproducibility. These substantive gains and documentation losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
